chapter.title: Chapter 1
chapter.openingCardText: Если вселенная действительно бесконечна, то эта история основана на реальных событиях.
chapter.endingCardText: Без тебя #— бессмыслен весь мой труд.

backgroundImage.label: Ocnoer's Chamber - Storm
backgroundImage.altText: A dark medieval tower chamber with a large arched window overlooking a rainy castle courtyard at night

characterPool.name: Pascal
characterPool.bio: Lord Pascal Varron, The Hand of the King in Valestria

dialogue.text: Rain fell steadily against the stone walls of the tower.
Ocnoer stood beside the narrow window of her chambers, watching the courtyard far below.
Torches flickered in the rain, their reflections trembling across the wet stones.
Men moved quickly through the yard, speaking louder than usual.
The castle had been restless all night.
Her cat lay near the hearth
A knock came at the door.
Ocnoer did not turn.
The door opened. Her cat rose at once and slipped out into the corridor.
Her maid entered, bowed her head, and spoke softly.
My lady, the Hand of the King is here.
Then she withdrew.
Lord Pascal stepped into the chamber and waited.
Ocnoer kept her eyes on the rain.
How is my father?
Pascal answered with care.
The maesters say His Grace has grown weaker, Princess.
Ocnoer was silent a moment.
Has he worsened much? Is he dying?
Pascal lowered his head.
Princess, your lady mother asks that you come to him.
Ocnoer stood still.
That was answer enough.
Then she turned from the window.

characterPool.name: Mother
characterPool.bio: Queen Maelis Valamere of House Cassivar in Valestria, a lady wife to King Maedric Valamere

characterPool.name: Pascal
characterPool.bio: Lord Pascal Varron, The Hand of the King in Valestria

dialogue.text: The corridor felt colder than she remembered.
Or perhaps everything felt colder now.
They stopped before the doors to the king’s chambers. Lord Pascal entered first.
He announced softly...
Princess Ocnoer
Her mother stood beside the bed, pale in the candlelight.
The Queen said with a tired nod...
Thank you, Pascal
The Hand bowed and withdrew.
Ocnoer stepped forward.
Her father lay beneath white linens, breathing slowly, each breath shallower than the last.
The maesters whispered among themselves nearby, their voices low and careful.
Come, you must be brave.
Ocnoer looked at her mother, then at her father
Her father’s eyes remained closed.
Perhaps he could hear them.
Perhaps he could not.
She leaned closer.
Ocnoer said softly...
Father,
Though the words caught painfully in her throat...
Stay with us… a little longer.
The maesters fell silent.
Her mother noticed and gestured for them to leave. One by one they slipped from the room.
Her mother whispered...
Ocnoer,
But Ocnoer barely heard her.
Still, she leaned down and kissed her father’s forehead.
A tear slipped from her eye and fell across his cheek.
I will be brave,
I will be brave for you, father

characterPool.name: Mother
characterPool.bio: Queen Maelis Valamere of House Cassivar in Valestria, a lady wife to King Maedric Valamere

dialogue.text: The carriage moved slowly through the streets of Valestria.
Rain had stopped, but the sky remained grey and heavy above the city. People lined the roads as the royal procession passed.
Some knelt. Some wept. Others only watched in silence.
Ocnoer sat beside her mother in the carriage, hands folded in her lap.
For a long time neither of them spoke.
Finally the Queen said quietly...
Your father loved this city more than anything.
Ocnoer kept her eyes on the window.
He always said the people of Valestria were stubborn,
But loyal.
Ocnoer watched a woman in the crowd clutching a small child to her chest.
Do you think they will remember him kindly?
Her mother looked at her.
Yes,
But kings are remembered in many ways.
Ocnoer hesitated.
Mother… must I still go to Mirath?
The Queen did not answer immediately.
The realm needs peace...
Ocnoer lowered her eyes.
"I know"
A rider appeared beside the carriage.
Prince Lucair of Mirath.
He rode easily through the mud, rain darkening the shoulders of his cloak.
He and his father, King Aedric, had come for her father's funeral—and to ask for her hand.
Everyone knew it.
Ocnoer searched herself for some feeling as she watched him ride beside them.
She found none she could name.
Perhaps that did not matter.
Lucair glanced toward the carriage and their eyes nearly met.
Ocnoer quickly pulled the curtain closed.

characterPool.name: Vaelan
characterPool.bio: King Vaelan Valamere in Valestria, uncle to Princess Ocnoer

dialogue.text: Thousands had gathered upon the hill for the burial.
The wind tugged gently at the black banners as the kingsguard carried the king’s body forward.
Ocnoer stood among the royal family.
Her uncle stood nearby.
Prince Vaelan Valamere.
King now, by right.
He noticed her watching and stepped closer.
You should not stand alone today.
I’m not alone,
My mother is here.
Vaelan gave a small, tired smile.
That is not what I meant.
Ocnoer looked toward the bier where her father lay.
It feels strange,
Seeing him like this.
Vaelan’s expression softened.
Your father was a great man,
And a good brother to me.
Ocnoer hesitated.
You will be king now.
Yes.
You will be very busy.
Vaelan chuckled quietly.
I suppose I will.
He placed a hand briefly on her shoulder.
You will always have a place here, Ocnoer. Remember that.
She nodded.
But she knew she would soon leave.
Mirath awaited her.
And Princess Lina.
Lina had always been kind to her.
"Perhaps life there would not feel so lonely."
She tried to believe that.

backgroundImage.label: Valestria's Corridor
backgroundImage.altText: Dim corridor with warm doorway glow

characterPool.name: Zareen
characterPool.bio: Queen Zareen Valamere of House Saffryn from Azdara in Valestria, a lady wife to the new King Vaelan Valamere in Valestria

dialogue.text: Later that evening, the castle had begun to stir again.
The Small Council had gathered to discuss matters of the realm. As a princess, Ocnoer had never been invited to such meetings—her title did not permit her attendance there.
She had never minded until now.

Now she could only picture her uncle inside those chambers, surrounded by men already pressing him with questions of trade, borders, and mourning, as though grief itself could be arranged between matters of state.
"He has not even had a full day to grieve."
And yet the castle was already slipping back into its old habits.
Ocnoer walked quietly through the corridor toward her chambers when she heard laughter behind a half-open door.
It was soft, low, and immediately wrong against the hush of the night.
Then came voices.
She slowed at once.
One of them she recognized immediately.
"Zareen."
Her uncle’s wife.
Ocnoer stopped beside the wall, listening despite herself.
She should have kept walking. She knew that.
Nothing good ever came from lingering near half-open doors. Still, she remained where she was.
Zareen was not alone.
A man stood somewhere deeper in the chamber, hidden from view.
Ocnoer did not recognize his voice, but there was something in it that made her uneasy at once.
A fine knight, your husband,
Brave enough for songs. But men like that were not made to rule.
Ocnoer frowned.
The words were reckless enough. The tone was worse.
You always speak as though you know men better than they know themselves.
He sees duty,
Crowns, councils, enemies. He sees what is expected of him...
And not what stands before him.
Dearest Zareen, you're such a clever woman
Silence followed, and in that silence Ocnoer felt her fingers tighten around her sleeve.
You are bold tonight.
You look too lovely tonight for me to be cautious.
Zareen gave a soft laugh.
It was that laugh, more than anything, that made Ocnoer’s stomach turn.
You should be careful.
Send him east,
Ocnoer went still.
There was a pause inside the chamber.
And let me handle Vaelan.
Ocnoer’s breath caught.
"God."
Those were not careless words, nor words spoken for sport. And yet Zareen did not stop him.
There was only the faint rustle of fabric from within the room, as though she had shifted where she stood.
Ocnoer stared at the thin strip of dim light spilling across the corridor stones and tried to make sense of what she was hearing.
The man remained hidden deeper within the chamber, beyond the torchlight, and the stone walls bent his voice just enough to make it impossible to place.
Then, like something foul rising from deep water, the old rumor returned.
"Tarek Kharaz."
The Azdaran knight her uncle had killed in a duel years ago.
"No."
She had always despised those whispers.

They were the kind of poison courts loved best—half scandal, half fantasy. That Zareen had loved another man. That Jorren had been Tarek’s son. That everyone had known and no one had dared speak it aloud.
"Court filth. Nothing more."
But now she stood outside a half-open door, listening to a man speak of her uncle as though his marriage were an inconvenience and his life a matter to be arranged, and Zareen was not silencing him.
"Was it always like this?"
The man spoke again, too low for her to catch the words, and Zareen answered with something softer still.
Ocnoer could not hear the rest.
Footsteps sounded from the far end of the corridor. Ocnoer straightened at once, stepped back from the door, and forced herself onward before anyone could find her there.
She kept her pace even until she had turned the corner, and only then did she let out the breath she had been holding.
Her heart was beating too fast.
"I cannot leave this unheard."
Her uncle sat in council while danger moved quietly through his own halls.
"I must warn him."
Morning came sooner than she expected.
Ocnoer woke to the sound of someone moving quietly through her chamber.
Elira...
Unfortunately,
And worse—you are awake too.
Ocnoer opened her eyes at that and found her friend standing by the bed with a basin of warm water.
At the foot of the bed, her black cat sat watching the room with the grave suspicion of a much older creature.
Its tail flicked once.
Elira glanced at it.
Your cat has been staring at me as though I’ve committed some personal offense.
Ocnoer’s hand moved at once to stroke the cat’s back.
For the first time that morning, the corner of her mouth nearly lifted.
What hour is it?
Late enough that your prince is already in the garden.
He is what?
Waiting.
"This is a nightmare."
Ocnoer sat up with a sigh.
The heaviness of yesterday returned at once—the funeral, the silence in the castle, the voices she had heard in the corridor. For a moment she said nothing.
You needn’t go looking delighted,
He will survive if you look solemn.
I always look solemn.
Well, not always. Only when spoken to by princes, septas, and old women.
Ocnoer reached down and scratched {{ cat_name }} lightly beneath the chin.
That almost earned her a smile.
Elira moved to the chest and began sorting through gowns.
Choose your dress.
This one.
As Elira helped her dress, her fingers worked quickly and neatly, with the ease of habit.
Do I look terrible?
You look as though your father died yesterday,
Any man with sense would know the difference.
Elira stepped behind her to fix her hair.
For a moment there was only the quiet pull of the brush.
What if he expects me to know what to say?
Elira met her eyes in the mirror.
He is the one who came to court you. Let him struggle.
Ocnoer looked at her reflection.
That is terrible advice.
It is excellent advice. Smile once, speak little, and let him think himself clever.
Ocnoer laughed softly despite herself.
There she is.
She pinned back the last strand and stepped away to look at her.
You look beautiful.
You are my friend. You are obliged to say that.
No. If you looked awful, I wouldn’t let you out of this room.
That made Ocnoer laugh again, properly this time, and the sound surprised them both.
It faded quickly, but not unhappily.
Are you nervous?
Ocnoer hesitated, then nodded once.
Elira took her hand and squeezed it.
Good, that means you are not foolish.
Ocnoer rolled her eyes, but she did not let go of Elira’s hand at once.
Then at last she stood.
Well, if I must suffer, come with me as far as the door.
Gladly.
Together they crossed the chamber and stepped out into the morning.

backgroundImage.label: Garden - Valestria
backgroundImage.altText: Serene garden with horses at dawn

dialogue.text: The garden was cool and still.
Two men stood near the fountain, speaking together.
Prince Lucair.
Beside him stood Prince Razin Saffryn of Azdara—Queen Zareen’s younger brother.
They were deep in conversation.
Ocnoer paused for a moment before approaching.
The fountain ran softly between them, its water bright in the morning light.
Then Lucair turned.
The conversation ended at once.
When Razin noticed her, he bowed lightly toward Ocnoer.
My princess.
At the sound of his voice, a sharp thought rose in her at once.
"Was it him?"
For a heartbeat she saw again the half-open door, the thin strip of dim light across the corridor stones, the man hidden deeper in one of the castle’s chambers.
But as Razin straightened, the thought faltered.
"No."
His Azdaran accent was plain now that she heard him properly.
And besides, whatever poison courts liked to whisper, surely a brother would not speak to his own sister as that man had spoken to Zareen.
Razin’s gaze shifted briefly to Lucair.
There was amusement in it, but little warmth.
I leave you to gentler company, my friend.
Lucair’s expression did not change.
Then Razin inclined his head once to Ocnoer.
Princess.
With that, he turned and walked away down the garden path.
Ocnoer watched him go.
For some reason, she found herself watching until he had vanished beyond the hedges.
Only then did she look back at Lucair.
Good morrow,
My princess.
His voice carried the same calm confidence she had noticed the day before at her father’s funeral.
Then his expression softened.
My deepest condolences for your loss.
Ocnoer lowered her head slightly.
Thank you, my prince.
For a moment no one spoke.
Water moved quietly behind them.
The morning was bright, but the castle still felt shadowed by yesterday.
Lucair glanced toward the fountain.
I hoped the morning air might bring you some comfort,
Castles can feel heavy after such days.
Ocnoer gave a small nod.
They do.
He studied her for a moment.
I was going to tell you that you look beautiful this morning…
Ocnoer looked at him then.
She said nothing, but the faintest smile touched her mouth.
Lucair’s eyes rested on her a moment longer.
Ocnoer glanced toward the gravel paths winding through the garden.
You and Prince Razin seemed at ease with one another.
The words left her before she could decide whether to keep them.
Lucair looked toward the path where Razin had gone.
At ease?
No,
Not quite.
He spoke mildly, but his tone held something cool beneath it.
Mirath and Azdara have spent too many years testing one another’s borders to breed ease.
Yet you were speaking privately.
Yes.
He did not explain further.
Ocnoer waited.
At last Lucair looked back at her.
Princes are often made to speak politely with men they would rather not trust.
Ocnoer thought of the voices in the corridor the night before.
Of hidden danger and smiling words.
The thought made her chest tighten.
Lucair followed her gaze toward the horses.
Would you ride with me?
Only within the outer grounds. We can turn back whenever you wish.
Ocnoer hesitated.
She had not ridden since before her father fell ill.
Some part of her wanted to refuse simply because the morning already felt too full.
But another part wanted movement.
Distance.
A little space from stone walls and closed doors and everything the castle now seemed to contain.
She nodded.
Lucair approached the horses and took the reins of one, offering it to her.
His movements were practiced and easy.
Lina always spoke kindly of you.
At the mention of Lina, something in Ocnoer eased.
Did she?
She never spoke a word of you.
For the briefest moment, Lucair seemed almost amused.
Then a slight smile touched his mouth.
No?
I can’t imagine why.
I missed her yesterday...
You will see her soon, princess.
Ocnoer felt a small flicker of comfort at that.
She mounted.
Lucair watched to make sure she was settled, then mounted his own horse.
He brought it beside hers.
For a moment neither of them moved.
The fountain murmured softly behind them.
Then Lucair glanced toward the open garden gate.
Come,
Let us ride.
By the time Ocnoer returned from her ride with Lucair, the day had left her quieter than before.
They had spoken of Mirath, of marriage, and of the life waiting for her there. More than once he had spoken of her future as though it were already settled beyond question.
"Queen."
The word still sat strangely in her thoughts.
Before evening came, Prince Lucair and his father departed Valestria for Mirath.
Not long after, a servant came to summon Ocnoer to dine with her uncle and his family.

backgroundImage.label: Grand Hall - Valestria
backgroundImage.altText: Twilight feast in a grand hall

characterPool.name: Vaelan
characterPool.bio: King Vaelan Valamere in Valestria, uncle to Princess Ocnoer

characterPool.name: Zareen
characterPool.bio: Queen Zareen Valamere of House Saffryn from Azdara in Valestria, a lady wife to the new King Vaelan Valamere in Valestria

dialogue.text: The evening meal was laid in a long chamber within the royal apartments, where the last golden light of day spilled through tall windows and stretched across silver dishes, dark bread, roasted fowl, stewed vegetables, and cups of watered wine.
But the room itself was far from calm.
Vaelan and Zareen were already seated at the table when Ocnoer entered.
Whatever had begun before her arrival had already sharpened into open strain.
Jorren and Aren were eating in uneasy silence, though Jorren looked far more entertained than concerned.
Vaelan noticed Ocnoer first.
Forcing some calm into his voice, he said...
Ocnoer,
Come. Sit.
Ocnoer inclined her head and moved toward the table.
As she took her seat beside Aren, she glanced between Vaelan and Zareen.
What has happened?
Aren lowered the piece of bread in his hand and answered at once.
Mother does not want Father to go east.
Jorren gave a small, unpleasant laugh.
No,
Because apparently it is not worth risking a king’s life merely to see your little wedding in Mirath.
Zareen’s eyes cut sharply to him.
Jorren.
Ocnoer looked at him steadily.
For something so unimportant, Jorren, you seem remarkably eager to be noticed through it.
Jorren’s mouth tightened.
Before he could answer, Zareen spoke.
It is not the wedding, princess,
It is the tourney.
Her gaze shifted back to Vaelan.
You are going east with Queen Maelis and Ocnoer regardless. That is understood. But there is no reason for you to ride in the lists as well.
Vaelan folded his arms.
I will not have the realm whispering that its king is afraid to ride.
The realm has just buried one king,
It can survive whispers better than another funeral.
Aren lowered his eyes to his plate.
Even Jorren fell quiet for a moment.
Vaelan gave a short, humorless breath.
You speak as though I am some old man fit only for councils and chairs.
I speak as though you are no longer merely a knight,
You are king now. Start valuing your life accordingly.
For a moment the room was still.
Ocnoer watched Zareen closely.
There was nothing playful in her now. Nothing secretive. Nothing that matched the woman Ocnoer had heard behind that half-open door.
She sounded only angry.
Only afraid.
"Is she trying to protect him?"
The thought unsettled Ocnoer more than if Zareen had sounded cruel.
Vaelan’s jaw tightened.
I am not hiding behind a crown because my wife has grown anxious.
Zareen’s expression turned colder.
And I am not watching my husband throw himself at lances to satisfy wounded vanity.
That struck cleanly.
Vaelan stared at her for a moment.
Then he turned away, sharp with anger.
I will ride,
The matter is ended.
And without another word, he left the hall.
The door shut hard behind him.
Silence settled over the table.
Zareen remained still for a moment, one hand resting beside her cup.
Eat.
Aren obeyed at once.
Yes, mother.
Ocnoer reached for her cup, though her appetite had already faded.
Jorren tore off another piece of bread.
At least Mirath may be worth the journey to someone...
Zareen did not look at him.
Jorren.
But Jorren, as ever, did not know when to stop.
He glanced at Ocnoer.
Perhaps Prince Lucair is not so eager for the wedding as for what comes after it.
Aren looked up in startled discomfort.
Ocnoer turned to Jorren slowly.
Her answer came at once, colder than anger.
Каждый думает в меру своей испорченности.
The Frostgardian words fell into the room like iron.
Jorren frowned, not understanding.
Zareen's gaze sharpened at once.
You will not speak to my son like that at this table.
Ocnoer held her eyes.
Then perhaps your son should not speak like that of my betrothed.
For a moment neither of them moved.
You are a guest in this city now, princess. Do not forget yourself.
The words stung more than they should have.
"Guest."
Not daughter of the late king. Not niece. Not family.
Only a guest.
Ocnoer rose from her seat.
I have lost my appetite.
Aren glanced up at her with quiet unease.
Jorren said nothing now.
Zareen only lifted her cup, her face once more smooth and unreadable.
Ocnoer inclined her head the barest amount and turned away.
When she stepped out into the corridor, the light beyond the western windows had deepened into gold and amber.
Her uncle had gone in anger.
Zareen had sounded like a woman trying to keep him alive.
And Ocnoer still did not know what to believe.
But one thing was clear now.
She could not leave Valestria without speaking to Vaelan first.
"I must find him."

backgroundImage.label: Balcony - Valestria
backgroundImage.altText: Golden sunset over Valestria's stone city

characterPool.name: Vaelan
characterPool.bio: King Vaelan Valamere in Valestria, uncle to Princess Ocnoer

dialogue.text: Ocnoer found Vaelan on the castle balcony overlooking the city.
Sunset lay over Valestria in gold and amber. The river below caught the light like fire.
He stood with one hand on the stone railing. When he heard her steps, he turned.
I thought you might come.
I did not wish to intrude.
You are not intruding.
For a moment neither spoke.
I spoke harshly at supper.
You were angry.
That is no excuse.
His voice was quieter now. Tired.
I have had too many voices in my ear and too little patience for any of them.
He looked back over the city.
That is a poor quality in a king.
Ocnoer stepped beside him at the railing.
Was Lucair good to you today?
Yes...
But the word came with hesitation.
Vaelan glanced at her.
Ocnoer lifted her hand.
The ring caught the last light.
He gave me this.
Vaelan looked at it, and some of the strain left his face.
Then he means to honor the match,
That is as it should be.
Ocnoer lowered her hand.
The ring felt heavier after that.
She kept her eyes on the city.
Must you truly go to Mirath?
Vaelan stiffened.
Not you, Ocnoer,
Do not begin this as well.
I did not mean—
I know what you meant,
I have heard it from Zareen already, and enough from myself besides.
It is not only that.
He turned to her.
What then?
Ocnoer hesitated only a moment.
The other night, I heard something.
His expression tightened.
In the corridor,
One of the chamber doors was half open. I heard Zareen speaking with a man.
Ocnoer...
I know how it sounds. I should have walked on. I know that.
But I heard him say you should be sent east.
Vaelan exhaled through his nose.
Zareen speaks privately with her brother often enough.
I do not think it was Prince Razin.
And why not?
I heard Prince Razin’s voice in the garden this morning. It was not the same.
Vaelan shook his head.
Voices change through stone and doors.
He said more than that.
Vaelan said nothing.
Ocnoer pressed on.
He said you should be sent east, and that he would handle you.
Vaelan looked away toward the city.
When he answered, impatience had returned.
This is about the lists.
What?
The tourney,
Whoever he was, he was speaking like a man who thinks too highly of his own lance. Half the fools riding east already imagine themselves glorious.
He did not sound like a fool boasting.
Vaelan turned back to her.
Ocnoer opened her mouth.
Enough of this.
Then she closed it.
Because she could not answer that without sounding exactly as he already feared she would.
Alarmed. Childish. Full of whispers and shadows.
Vaelan’s voice remained controlled now, but there was steel in it.
You have had a hard day. A hard week. You are grieving. You are soon to leave your home.
Do not let every half-heard word become danger in your mind.
Ocnoer felt something in her chest tighten.
I was only trying to warn you.
And I am telling you to let it rest.
The words were not loud.
But they struck harder than if they had been.
For a moment neither of them spoke.
The city bells rang faintly again in the distance.
Ocnoer turned her face away before he could read too much in it.
Below them, the rooftops of Valestria blurred softly in the last light.
"He will not hear me."
The wind moved between them.
When Vaelan spoke again, his voice had changed.
Some of the hardness had gone out of it.
I spoke with Lucair before he left,
I asked him that after the marriage, he should take you to Naitō for a visit.
She turned to him at once.
Naitō?
Yes.
Something changed in her face then.
She had always loved the old tales of the East. Naito was one of those names that had lived in her mind longer than she could remember.
You asked him that?
I did.
For one brief moment, the future held something other than duty.
Then the feeling thinned.
Vaelan saw the change in her face.
Take what peace you can from Valestria while it is still yours to take.
That struck deeper than she wished it to.
Her gaze moved over the rooftops, the river, the towers touched by the last of the sun.
Vaelan’s voice was quieter when he spoke again.
Mirath comes soon enough.
Ocnoer did not trust herself to answer.
They stood together above the city as the last light faded.
Valestria fell behind them at last.
With King Vaelan and Queen Maelis Regent, Ocnoer rode east toward Mirath.
After days upon the road, they came to Hollowpine.

characterPool.name: Mother
characterPool.bio: Queen Maelis Valamere of House Cassivar in Valestria, a lady wife to King Maedric Valamere

characterPool.name: Vaelan
characterPool.bio: King Vaelan Valamere in Valestria, uncle to Princess Ocnoer

dialogue.text: Hollowpine stood where the roads of three kingdoms met.
Tall pines rose around Hollowpine beneath a clear sky.
Sunlight lay across the cobbled road between steep-roofed timber houses, and a wooden watchtower stood beyond the gate among the trees.
The air smelled of pine, earth, and smoke.
The royal party was met just beyond the entrance.
A man in Hollowpine colors stepped forward and bowed low before Vaelan.
Y-Your Grace.
Vaelan dismounted.
Where is Arys?
The man kept his head lowered.
L-Lord Arys rode out to the eastern crossing before your arrival, Your Grace.
The last r-rains damaged part of the road, and he w-went to see it himself.
And you are?
Ser Coren, Your Grace.
C-Castellan of Hollowpine.
By then the carriage door had been opened.
Queen Maelis stepped down first.
Ocnoer followed beside her, carrying the wicker basket with {{ cat_name }} inside.
{{ cat_name }} had not been still since they entered the pines.
Queen Maelis looked toward Ser Coren.
Then let us be grateful he thought first of the road,
A ruined crossing would delay us more than a missed greeting.
Ser Coren bowed again.
Yes, Your Grace.
Vaelan said nothing for a moment.
Then he gave a short nod.
We will remain for the night.
Everything has been p-prepared, Your Grace.
Ocnoer stood beside the carriage while servants moved among the horses and baggage.
The village looked ordinary enough.
Road-worn. Weathered. Busy.
Yet something in it felt strained.
Her gaze drifted toward a pair of men crossing near the gate. She would not have looked at them twice, if not for the sound of their voices.
Azdaran.
Only faintly.
Only enough to catch at her attention.
A little later, from farther off, she heard it again in another voice.
Her fingers tightened slightly on the handle of the basket.
But Hollowpine stood at the meeting place of kingdoms. Men passed through such a place from everywhere. Traders. Riders. Sellswords. Messengers.
An Azdaran accent here meant little.
Or should have.
Inside the basket, {{ cat_name }} shifted again.
Queen Maelis glanced toward it.
Still unhappy?
